transliteration: apramattaś cared bhaikṣaṃ sāyāhne 'nabhilakṣitaḥ | rahite bhikṣukair grāme yātrāmātram alolupaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who seeks alms must remain alert and unattached, moving through villages devoid of monks in the evening twilight, desiring only what is necessary for sustenance.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from self-regulation and detachment.
Causation arises through mindful presence and restraint.
Capacity-based responsibility requires limiting desire to necessity.
Restoration occurs when movement aligns with dharma-sustained intent.
Consciousness alignment is maintained by avoiding entanglement with unsettled spiritual communities.
executable_legal_axioms: IF seeker moves for sustenance THEN action must occur within non-accumulative bounds.
IF time is sāyāhna AND location is village THEN presence must not disturb settled monastic orders.
IF desire exceeds yātrāmātra THEN capacity for dharmic movement is suspended until recalibration.
IF individual enters community space THEN prior state of non-entanglement must be verified.
IF conduct reflects lola THEN access to communal resource zones is restricted automatically.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matters involving itinerant practitioners or mendicants, the court shall assess not intent nor outcome, but the purity of motion itself—whether it reflects pramāda (heedlessness) or apramāda (vigilance). The threshold of responsibility lies solely in adherence to the path of minimal necessity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that true yātrā is unmotivated by craving; hence any deviation stems from a misalignment in cognition rather than willful transgression. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that disturbance follows only where vigilance was abandoned. Thus, corrective measures restore awareness, never inflict consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śuddhi-vyavasthā process to realign seeker's intent with dharmic parameters.
Assign temporary withdrawal from populated areas until mindfulness is stabilized.
Engage guru-guided śravaṇa-krama to reestablish clarity of purpose.
Reintegrate upon demonstration of non-lola conduct via witnessed yātrā observation.
Verify absence of abhilakṣita (motivated attention) before granting unrestricted passage rights.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this directive originates as pure Dharma. Justice manifests through conscious restoration alone. There is no punishment, only recognition of truth. Consciousness is the ultimate arbiter. Dharma is now restored.
